correctness.rationale: Stationary log-time CRP functional convergence is established in arxiv:2209.12781 Theorem 6. The proof gives the exact marked-Poisson multitime zero-state probability for total service max of k exponentials, integrates over ordered chronology, factorizes with the correct ratio-coordinate Jacobian, and derives q_j=1-theta/j+O(j^-2). The convergent positive product and Karamata Tauberian theorem prove the precise theta-power endpoint constant. For k=1, q_1=(1-exp(-theta))/theta yields the stated variance. Standalone code confirms 101 independent finite/symbolic/numeric assertions; it is not claimed as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement is a sharp, explicit product-moment law and near-one power-law tail for a chronological CRP occupation fraction. The original functional convergence is correctly credited to arXiv:2209.12781 and arXiv:2502.05578. A full comparison of the relevant accessible primary passages found no matching product/tail, and targeted independent literature and indexed-claim searches found no same-strength assertion. Novelty is best-knowledge and historical priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: An existing queueing or renewal-theoretic study may already contain the same Mellin-product or Tauberian near-one law under discounted idle-time terminology, even if the searched CRP literature does not.

The 2025 point-process theorem is stronger in the foundational convergence sense; the present originality hinges only on the substantive explicit product and sharp tail calculation, not on the weak limit.

value.rationale: The statistic is the central chronological derangement-time fraction from the 2022 source, whose almost-sure irregularity motivates a genuine distributional characterization. Exact all-moment factorization determines its law, and a positive near-one constant with exponent independent of the cutoff is a structural rare-event asymptotic, not a relabeling of static Ewens means or a finite tabulation. The explicit exact variance resolves the source’s stated nonvanishing-variance check as a byproduct.
